summary: Thirteen experiments consumed 96.6 minutes, including 7 compute-bound experiments. The 71.83-minute synthesis-only conformance task dominated elapsed time; the longest listed compute-bound task took 20.4 minutes, and the locked task-conditioned GPU-idle indicator is false.
bottlenecks_identified: The 71.83-minute synthesis-only adaptive operations ABI conformance path dominated the 96.6-minute milestone.

Among the listed compute-bound paths, the 20.4-minute causal-pair embedding extraction across three model families exceeded the 0.9-minute closed-loop visual probing task; the timing data does not explain either duration because no phase breakdown is supplied.
Disk-mtime reconstruction provides task-level durations but no task-correlated phase, GPU, loaded-model-count, or runner trace, limiting causal efficiency analysis.
improvements_suggested: Add resumable checkpoints and content-addressed reuse to the long synthesis-only ABI conformance path.
Persist phase timings and sampled GPU utilization under the same task identifier for every compute-bound run.
Record simultaneous loaded-model count and selected runner; dispatch DualGPURunner only for genuine concurrent multi-model work.
Persist conductor event timings independently of git commits so milestone accounting does not depend on disk-mtime reconstruction.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Make ABI conformance synthesis resumable and cache unchanged inputs.
Add task-correlated phase and GPU telemetry to compute-bound execution.
Capture model concurrency and runner selection, with dual-GPU dispatch limited to genuine parallel multi-model work.
meta_reflection: The evidence ranks task-level elapsed time but does not expose phases or tie the GPU snapshot to task intervals. It therefore supports identifying the long paths, but not claiming causal GPU inefficiency or a missed parallel runner.
